acip: ,SEMS CAN RNAMS KYI GNAS LUGS NI, ,SEMS DANG DUS MNYAM GNAS DUS NAS, ,YE SANGS RGYAS CIG YIN PA LA, ,'ON KYANG GLO BUR DRI MAS BSGRIBS,
wylie: sems can rnams kyi gnas lugs ni, ,sems dang dus mnyam gnas dus nas, ,ye sangs rgyas cig yin pa la, ,'on kyang glo bur dri mas bsgribs
english: The way of all things Lies here within people; It has lived there part & parcel With their minds since minds began— This is the one primordial Buddha That each of them already is; It's just that this Buddha is veiled By impurities that are not at all Innate parts of the mind. There's some talk going around about how we are already a Buddha inside of us, so we should just relax and let our natural Buddha out.  This is a gross and, eventually, very harmful misunderstanding of the idea of “Buddha nature.” That is, all things possess their inherent emptiness, or the lack of being anything except the end product of our mental seeds, planted by how we treat other people.  This emptiness—in the case of each individual one of us—will remain with us even after we turn into a being who can see everything that is, was, and ever will be in the whole universe. Only in this sense, there is within each of us what will inevitably—in time—become a fully enlightened being.  But we still need to work hard to become the entire package! The final comment here about impurities not being an inherent part of our mind is important.  The best part of the Buddha that we will become is, as we have just shown, an inherent part of our being; but the negative parts of our being are perfectly impermanent and will inevitably be cleaned out.
